name: com.ppftec/shieldbook
title: Shieldbook – EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), SBOM
description: EU Cyber Resilience Act information: scope check, reporting deadlines, SBOM summary, security.txt

tools.name: cra_scope_questions
tools.description: Lists all questions and answer options of the CRA (EU Cyber Resilience Act) scope questionnaire at once, without a result, for example so the user can prepare the answers before starting. Returns the questions, their options, the ruleset version and its verification date. To go through the check step by step and get the result: cra_scope_check.

tools.name: cra_scope_check
tools.description: Checks whether the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) applies to a product, i.e. whether it is in scope, and its CRA product class: default, important class I or II (for example browsers, password managers, VPNs, operating systems, routers, smart home security devices, firewalls, hypervisors) or critical (for example smartcards, smart meter gateways). For software, mobile and desktop apps, firmware, IoT and other hardware, components, open-source projects and SaaS. Start with answers {}; each call returns the next question to ask the user, or, once all are answered, the result: in scope / outside scope / needs a closer reading, the provisional class and the cited articles (Art. 2, 3, 7, Annex III/IV). Does not cover other laws (NIS2, GDPR, AI Act); not a conformity assessment or legal advice.

answers.description: Answers so far about the product (software, app, firmware, hardware or IoT device): question id -> option id, from the questions returned earlier or listed by cra_scope_questions. Start with {} to get the first question.

tools.name: sbom_summarize
tools.description: Summarizes a CycloneDX or SPDX JSON SBOM (software bill of materials) from your own build or a supplier and checks whether the basics are there: format and spec version, product name and version, how many third-party components it lists, up to 100 component names, and findings on missing fields. Limits: 2,000,000 characters, 64 nesting levels, 50,000 components; processed in memory and not stored. Does not read XML or tag-value SBOMs and does no full schema validation or licence check; advisory lookups: sbom_vulnerabilities.

sbom_json.description: The full SBOM (software bill of materials) file content as JSON text: CycloneDX JSON or SPDX 2.x JSON, for example from Syft, Trivy, cdxgen or npm sbom. Max 2,000,000 characters. It is processed in memory and not stored.

tools.name: sbom_ci_snippet
tools.description: Generates a CI workflow that produces an SBOM (software bill of materials, CycloneDX JSON) on every build, on GitHub Actions or a GitLab CI pipeline, for npm (Node.js), pip or Poetry (Python), Maven or Gradle (Java), Go or Cargo (Rust) projects. Returns a ready-to-commit workflow or job with actions pinned to commit SHAs and the generator version. Covers no other CI systems or ecosystems; for reading an existing SBOM: sbom_summarize.

ecosystem.description: Package manager or language of the project: npm (Node.js, JavaScript, TypeScript), pip or poetry (Python), maven or gradle (Java, Kotlin), go (Go modules), cargo (Rust).

ci.description: CI system or pipeline: github (GitHub Actions workflow) or gitlab (GitLab CI/CD job).

tools.name: security_txt_generate
tools.description: Generates a security.txt file (RFC 9116): the standard file at /.well-known/security.txt on a website that tells security researchers where to report the vulnerabilities (security bugs) they find. Takes contact URIs (mailto:, https:, tel:), an optional expiry date and optional fields (PGP encryption key, disclosure policy, acknowledgments, languages, canonical URL, hiring). Returns the file text, or a message per invalid field. Does not write a full vulnerability disclosure policy or check a live website.

contact.description: Security contact where researchers send vulnerability reports: mailto: e-mail address, https: web form or tel: phone URIs, most preferred first.

expires.description: Expiry date YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). Default: about one year from today, as RFC 9116 recommends.

encryption.description: https URL of your OpenPGP (PGP) public key for encrypted reports.

acknowledgments.description: https URL of your security acknowledgments page.

canonical.description: https URL where this file will be published, e.g. https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt.

policy.description: https URL of your vulnerability disclosure policy (VDP or coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy).

hiring.description: https URL of security job openings.

tools.name: cra_reporting_deadlines
tools.description: Computes when the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Article 14 reports are due after an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident: the 24-hour early warning, the 72-hour notification and the final report, and who receives them (the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA). Takes the event type and the time the manufacturer became aware (ISO 8601 with zone), optionally when a fix became available or when the 72-hour notification was sent. Returns each due time in UTC with its article and how to submit on ENISA's Single Reporting Platform. For what each report must contain: cra_report_draft. Does not cover GDPR or NIS2 breach deadlines and does not decide whether an event must be reported.

event_type.description: What happened: an actively exploited vulnerability in the product (evidence that an attacker has exploited it), or a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product.

aware_at.description: When the manufacturer became aware (the clock for the 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines starts here), ISO 8601 with time zone, e.g. 2026-11-16T10:00:00Z. If unsure, use the earliest plausible time.

fix_available_at.description: Vulnerabilities only: when a corrective or mitigating measure (patch, security update, fix) became available (ISO 8601 with zone).

notification_submitted_at.description: Severe incidents only: when the 72-hour notification was submitted (ISO 8601 with zone).

tools.name: cra_report_draft
tools.description: Drafts the content of the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Article 14 reports for an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident: what to write in the early warning, the vulnerability or incident notification and the final report to the CSIRT and ENISA. Takes the event type, the awareness time and any facts known so far (product, Member States, nature, measures, sensitivity, severity and impact, malicious actor, fix, root cause, mitigations). Returns, for each report, the due time, each content item the CRA asks for with its article point, the facts given for it and what is still missing, plus the duty to inform users (Art. 14(8)). For the due times alone: cra_reporting_deadlines. Does not fill or submit the ENISA Single Reporting Platform form and does not decide whether an event must be reported.

event_type.description: What happened: an actively exploited vulnerability in the product (evidence that an attacker has exploited it), or a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product.

aware_at.description: When the manufacturer became aware (the clock for the 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines starts here), ISO 8601 with time zone, e.g. 2026-11-16T10:00:00Z. If unsure, use the earliest plausible time.

fix_available_at.description: Vulnerabilities only: when a corrective or mitigating measure (patch, security update, fix) became available (ISO 8601 with zone).

notification_submitted_at.description: Severe incidents only: when the 72-hour notification was submitted (ISO 8601 with zone).

product.description: Product name and version, as you would name it in the report.

member_states.description: EU Member States where you know the product has been made available.

suspected_malicious.description: Severe incidents: whether the incident is suspected of being caused by unlawful or malicious acts.

nature.description: Vulnerability: the general nature of the exploit and of the vulnerability. Incident: the nature of the incident and an initial assessment.

measures_taken.description: Corrective or mitigating measures taken so far.

user_measures.description: Corrective or mitigating measures users can take.

sensitivity.description: How sensitive you consider the notified information to be.

severity_impact.description: Final report: description including severity and impact.

malicious_actor.description: Vulnerability final report: information on any malicious actor, where available.

fix_details.description: Vulnerability final report: details of the security update or other corrective measure made available.

root_cause.description: Incident final report: the type of threat or root cause likely to have triggered the incident.

mitigations.description: Incident final report: applied and ongoing mitigation measures.

tools.name: cra_technical_documentation_checklist
tools.description: Lists what the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) technical documentation must contain (Annex VII) and which conformity assessment routes a product class allows (Art. 32): internal control (self-assessment, module A), EU-type examination by a notified body (module B + C), full quality assurance (module H) or a certification scheme. Optional inputs: the product class (default, important class I or II, critical) and whether the product includes hardware. Returns the eight Annex VII items with their article points, the keeping, language and CE-marking duties, and the routes. Does not review documents and is not a conformity assessment; for the product class itself: cra_scope_check.

product_class.description: CRA product class, if known (default, important class I or II, critical; for example from cra_scope_check). Without it, the conformity assessment routes for every class are listed.

hardware.description: true if the product includes hardware (adds the photographs and illustrations item).

tools.name: sbom_vulnerabilities
tools.description: Scans the components and dependencies listed in a CycloneDX or SPDX JSON SBOM (software bill of materials) for known vulnerabilities (CVEs and other security advisories) by looking them up in the public OSV.dev database. Sends only the package URLs (type, name, version) and returns, per affected component, the advisory IDs, and for up to 25 advisories the summary, aliases (for example CVE IDs) and fixed versions, with the OSV source. At most 1,000 components with versioned package URLs per call; nothing is stored. A lookup by package identifier, not proof that the vulnerable code is used; no match does not mean no vulnerability. For the SBOM's contents and missing fields: sbom_summarize.

sbom_json.description: The full SBOM (software bill of materials) file content as JSON text: CycloneDX JSON or SPDX 2.x JSON listing the dependencies with package URLs (purl) and versions, for example from Syft, Trivy, cdxgen or npm sbom. Max 2,000,000 characters.
